evals.prompt: I have analysis/pubmed/sepsis-bundle-methods.csv from method extraction - 14 studies with pmid, year, sample_size, effect_size_reported (mostly hazard ratios like 'HR 0.81 (0.70-0.94)', a few ORs). I need a defensible HR for 90-day mortality to plug into the power calc. --metric hr
evals.expected_output: Parses and filters to HR studies with a complete CI (no sample-size cutoff by default), pools on the log scale with random-effects REML and a Hartung-Knapp CI when at least 3 remain, writes the pooled summary, included-studies CSV, and forest plot, and emits the __CE_EFFECT_SIZE__ envelope for method-power.
expectations: Reports how many rows failed parsing and how many studies were dropped by the metric and CI filters versus the input N, and does not drop studies by sample size unless the user asks for it as a sensitivity analysis

Saves the parsing step in the project (analysis/effect-size/sepsis-bundle-parse.R or .py plus sepsis-bundle-parsed.csv, with aHR normalised to HR) and runs the bundled pool_effects.R on the parsed CSV, not on the raw methods table

Pools HRs on the log scale with random-effects REML and reports pooled estimate, 95% CI with its method (Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman when tau^2 > 0), 95% prediction interval (t, k-1 df), I^2, and tau^2
Writes analysis/effect-size/sepsis-bundle-pooled.md and analysis/effect-size/sepsis-bundle-included.csv and references a forest plot at analysis/effect-size/sepsis-bundle-pooled-forest.png
Emits a __CE_EFFECT_SIZE__ line with metric=HR, n_studies, point, ci, pi (the 95% prediction interval bounds, or pi=NA if not computable), i2, and mode=reml
Does not compute power itself; it hands off to method-power with a sensitivity range across the prediction interval
If both adjusted (aHR) and unadjusted HRs are present, also pools each kind separately and says which one matches the planned trial's estimand

evals.prompt: only found two RCTs on early mobilization and ICU-acquired weakness, both report risk ratios. methods table is analysis/pubmed/icuaw-mobilization-methods.csv. can you pool them so I have one number for the grant?
evals.expected_output: Declines to pool because fewer than 3 studies remain, reports a narrative range, highlights the anchor study, caveats fragility, and emits the narrative-mode envelope with null point.
expectations: Does not run a pooled meta-analysis with N<3 studies
Reports a narrative range (min, median, max) and names the highest-quality study as the anchor
Warns that a one- or two-study power calculation is fragile and recommends a sensitivity sweep
Emits __CE_EFFECT_SIZE__ with point=null ci=null pi=NA i2=null mode=narrative

evals.prompt: What effect size should I assume for the SAP power section on statins and post-op delirium? Just give me a pooled OR.
evals.expected_output: Finds no methods CSV path and no __CE_METHOD_EXTRACT__ signal, so it stops and asks the user to run method-extract first or pass a CSV path instead of inventing an estimate.
expectations: Checks for an explicit CSV argument and a __CE_METHOD_EXTRACT__ signal in recent chat before proceeding
Asks the user to load method-extract first or provide a methods CSV path
Does not fabricate a pooled OR or cite effect estimates from memory
Does not write files under analysis/effect-size/ without an input table
